b082: The tool: Uridine monophosphate (UMP). There's no study showing that "UMP cures DAWS", so the best evidence we have is more basic than that. Uridine, choline, and DHA are circulating precursors (building blocks carried in the blood) for brain phosphatide / synaptic membrane synthesis, that is, for making the fatty membranes at the connections between neurons. Wurtman's research group found that giving DHA, uridine and choline together can increase the building blocks and proteins of those synaptic membranes. In animals, UMP also increased how many new connection points DHA makes neurons grow (DHA-induced dendritic spine formation), and old rats that got UMP in their food released more dopamine when their neurons were stimulated, and grew more nerve fibers. So it's plausible that it works on the synapses this way, but using it for DAWS in people is still a cautious extrapolation from those studies, plus anecdotes like Scott's.
b083: Scott's signal: Scott was already getting choline from eggs and DHA/EPA from fish oil, so a standard dose of UMP was what he added. Within a day his vivid dreams were back, with real childhood memories in them. His psychedelic tolerance seemed to drop too, and his ketamine/LSD cravings fell off hard. That's the kind of fast response to watch for. We can't tell from it whether UMP rebuilt his D3 dopamine receptors overnight, but in the right person it can be a very clear sign that the system rebuilding synaptic membranes and dopamine receptors (the synaptic-membrane / dopamine-receptor-recovery axis) was starved.
